title: Build bee config get, set, unset, explain and validate in Rust
action: Today `bee config get|set|unset|validate` refuse with 'not built into this binary' (registry entries carry an `unavailable` gap; router.rs ~404). Build them in Rust, plus a new `bee config explain`, so an agent never hand-edits .bee/config.json. Contract (decision b82c68d2; full prior-art digest in .bee/tmp/xia-forgent/config-prior-art.md; old Node code at `git show 5c62cad02^:packages/bee/bee.mjs` lines ~6276-6470): get --key <dotted> [--local] -> json {key, present, value|null, local, warning}; text `key = <json>` or `config get: "<key>" is not set.` (exit nonzero not required; match Node). set --key --value [--string] [--local] -> json {key, value}; value JSON-parsed, non-JSON kept as string, --string forces string; creates parent objects. unset --key [--local] -> {key, removed}; prunes empty parents. --local targets .bee/config.local.json and warns when the tracked file also sets the key. A missing file is created as {} on set; an existing file that is invalid JSON or not an object refuses the write with zero mutation. Writes go through fsutil::write_json_atomic. set and unset REFUSE (typed error, zero mutation) any key that is, or is inside, or contains a governed key the config write guard protects: team, herding.agents, herding.agent_command, hooks — reuse the guard's own governed-key list from hooks/write_guard/guards.rs (one home; do not copy the list) and give its remedy (the user edits this mapping directly). set refuses a write that adds a model-config validation problem when such a validator exists in Rust; if none exists, record that as a deviation. explain --key -> {key, effective, source: local|tracked|unset, tracked, local} and a short text form; `unset` source means the built-in default applies (name the docs/config-reference.md section in the text). validate -> reads both files, reports parse errors and model-config problems, exit nonzero on problems. Remove the `unavailable` gap for these verbs in the registry (regenerate registry_payload.json the way `bee dev` does it; find the generator) and register explain. Update docs/config-reference.md 'Setting values' section (lines 7-21) to document the verbs instead of telling readers to hand-edit. Tests (integration, driving the real binary in a temp repo): get/set/unset round trip with dotted keys and parent pruning; --local overlay and its warning; --string; invalid-file refusal leaves bytes unchanged; each governed key refused by set and unset with the file unchanged; explain source for local, tracked and unset. If you add a new public verb surface, run bee dev regen if the repo requires it (check the release-manifest obligation the cells add guard names).
verify_owner: main (feature close) — the worker never runs this
